Kapkaupungin Pöytävuorella (Table Mountain) tapahtuu ryöstöjä kävelyreittien varrella. Erityisesti liikkumista yksin tulee välttää.

Luottokortit kelpaavat maksuvälineenä useimmissa paikoissa, mutta niiden kopioiminen ja väärinkäyttö on myös yleistä. Turvarajat kannattaa pitää alhaisina.

Jos passisi katoaa tai varastetaan, tee siitä ilmoitus paikalliselle poliisiasemalle. Mikäli kohdemaassa ei ole Suomen edustustoa, hae hätämatkustusasiakirjaa (ETD = Emergency Travel Document) toisen EU-maan edustustosta.

Ota kopiot tärkeimmistä asiapapereista kuten passista ja lentolipuista. Säilytä ne erillään alkuperäisistä.

Liikenne

Liikenne on vasemmanpuoleista. Liikenteessä tulee olla valppaana. Auto-onnettomuudet ovat yleisiä. Auton ovet on syytä pitää aina lukittuina. Maanteillä tulee välttää turhia pysähtymisiä eikä tuntemattomia henkilöitä tule ottaa kyytiin. Etenkin moottoriteillä ja rampeilla kannattaa kiinnittää huomiota tiellä oleviin esineisiin sillä "spiking" (terävien esineiden teille laittaminen) sekä isojen kivien kerääminen esteeksi on yleistynyt. Autoilijan toivotaan pysähtyvän tielle renkaiden rikkouduttua, jonka jälkeen autoilija ryöstetään. Vaikka ajoneuvokanta on keskimäärin korkeatasoista ja tiet hyviä, on liikenteessä runsaasti myös huonokuntoisia ajoneuvoja, ajokortittomia ja päihtyneitä kuljettajia ja ajoneuvoja ilman liikennevakuutusta, jotka saattavat aiheuttaa riskitilanteita. Rattijuopumukseen ja ylinopeuteen kiinnitetään enenevässä määrin huomiota.

Maksullisten moottoriteiden tietullit eivät hyväksy kansainvälisiä luottokortteja, maksu suoritetaan käteisellä. (Paikalliset voivat hankkia nk. e-Tag tunnistimen, jolle ladataan saldoa etukäteen ja laite kiinnitetään auton tuulilasiin.)

Myös minibussien pysähtely matkustajien ottamiseksi ja pois laskemiseksi aiheuttaa vaaratilanteita, samoin jalankulkijoiden liikkuminen moottoriteillä varsinkin pimeän aikana, valaistus teillä on huono tai olematon.

Uber-taksien suhteen varovaisuus on tarpeen erityisesti Johannesburgissa ja Pretoriassa, varsinkin juna-asemien läheisyydessä. Kuljettajia kohtaan on tehty väkivaltaisia hyökkäyksiä, jolloin sivulliset tai matkustajat saattavat joutua osallisiksi.
Päällystämättömien teiden kunto (mm. luonnonpuistot) laskee huomattavasti sateiden aikaan ja nelivetoauto voi olla tarpeellinen.

Luonnonolot

Maan luonto on kaunis ja ilmasto miellyttävä ympäri vuoden. Talvikuukausina yöt saattavat olla kylmiä. Suomalaisen saattaa yllättää sisätilojen kylmyys. Sadekausi vaihtelee Kapkaupungin talvisateista Pretorian kesäsateisiin, jolloin sadekuurot saattavat olla rankkoja ja ukonilmat rajuja, etenkin Pretoriassa ja Johannesburgissa (Highveld).

Luonnonpuistoissa liikuttaessa on niiden sääntöjä ehdottomasti noudatettava.

Valtamerissä uidessa on syytä olla erityisen varovainen, koska vedenalaiset merivirrat saattavat olla hyvin voimakkaita ja viedä uimarin mukanaan.

Matkavakuutusta ajatellen on pidettävä mielessä, että yksityissairaaloissa vaaditaan yleensä maksua heti sairaalaan tuotaessa. Yleisissä sairaaloissa hoito on yleensä heikkotasoisempaa kuin yksityissairaaloissa. Mikäli saapuu maahan keltakuumealueelta tai tekee välilaskun keltakuumealueella ennen Etelä-Afrikkaan saapumista, vaaditaan keltakuumerokotustodistus, joka otettu vähintään 10 päivää ennen Etelä-Afrikkaan saapumista. Sääntöjä noudatetaan tarkasti.

Mobiililaitteisiin kannattaa ladata ilmainen mySOS-sovellus. Sovellus tarjoaa helpon ja nopean yhteyden paikalliseen hätäkeskukseen, joka puolestaan pystyy sovelluksen avulla paikantamaan soittajan sijainnin.

Maassa on runsaasti HIV-positiivista väestöä ja tartuntavaaraan liittyvää riskikäyttäytymistä tulee ehdottomasti välttää. Malariaa esiintyy varsinkin sadeaikana maan koillisosassa mukaan lukien Krugerin luonnonpuisto. Malarialääkityksen tarpeellisuudesta on syytä keskustella matkanjärjestäjän tai lääkärin kanssa. Myös muita tartuntatauteja kuten tuberkuloosia esiintyy melko runsaasti.

Vesijohtovesi on pääsääntöisesti juomakelpoista, mutta sitä ei suositella juotavaksi suuren metallipitoisuutensa vuoksi. Paikallisesti saattaa ajoittain esiintyä koleraa tai lavantautia ja Gauteng provinssissa se sisältää kaivostoiminnasta maahan päässeitä raskasmetalleja. Suurten kaupunkien kansainväliset sairaalat ja niiden tarjoamat palvelut ovat hyvin korkeatasoisia.

Avun saaminen luonnonpuistoissa tapahtuviin sairaskohtauksiin tai tapahturmiin saattaa viedä tavallista kauemmin aikaa etäisyyksien ja maasto-olosuhteiden vuoksi.

items.title: Git Patches Flaw That Lets Malicious Repositories Execute Code During Recursive Clones
items.summary: Classification: Severe, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Functional, CVSSv3.1: 7.5, CVEs: CVE-2026-113408, CVE-2026-114467, CVE-2026-114469, CVE-2026-105437, CVE-2026-114466, Summary: A flaw in Git can let a malicious repository run an attacker's code on a computer that clones it recursively, together with its submodules. The Git project fixed it this week in Git 2.56.1, with matching fixes for the 2.50 through 2.55 series in 2.50.2, 2.51.3, 2.52.1, 2.53.1, 2.54.1 and 2.55.1. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-111760, is an integer truncation in how Git handles its index. An extremely long path in a repository can pass Git's safety check, but Git then writes it to disk under a shorter name that an attacker can set to .git. This lets an attacker replace a submodule's .git file with a symbolic link to a folder holding malicious hooks or configuration. Hooks are programs Git runs at set points, so once Git uses that folder, the attacker's code can run. The fixed versions, listed in the Git project's release announcement, refuse such extremely long paths before their length can be cut short. See also: https://lore.kernel.org/git/xmqqh5hosgw5.fsf@gitster.g/

items.title: AI Harms Taxonomy
items.summary: Mapping the digital ways AI-enabled mechanisms can make consumers worse off, directly or indirectly. Plenty of people have made lists of the ways AI can go wrong. Very few of those lists tell you where different forces could get involved to stop the harms. So we built this around places to intervene. Each harm is traced through the points it passes on its way to the consumer, and each defense is attached at the point where it would actually have to be built. Doing it that way makes one thing very obvious: many of these harms are not ours to fix. They can only be fixed by the companies that make the models and run the products, and it seems better to say that than to pretend otherwise. Finally, this is a work in progress. Many entries list an evidence base, but some are still thin, and we are constantly reevaluating the structure of this taxonomy to keep pace with this fast-moving field. Your feedback is very welcome, especially if you think something is wrong.

items.title: SonicWall MFA Bypass Vulnerability Actively Exploited
items.summary: Classification: Important, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Proof-of-Concept, CVSSv3.1: 7.5, CVEs: CVE-2026-19868, Summary: Attackers are actively exploiting a flaw in the operating system that powers SonicWall firewalls to bypass multifactor authentication and gain access to the devices. The SSL VPN vulnerability enables attackers with valid credentials to bypass SAML - often used to facilitate single sign-on - as well as MFA, if it's tied to SAML, warns a security alert released Friday by SonicWall. The vulnerability in SonicWall Gen7 and Gen8 devices, assigned CVE-2026-19868, has a CVSS v3 score of 7.5. SonicOS versions up to and including 7.3.3-7015 and before, as well as 8.2.2-8015 and before, are vulnerable. SonicWall credited Ryan Harris of The Electronic Office, an IT services and consulting firm based in North Carolina, with discovering the flaw. Proof-of-concept code for exploiting CVE-2026-19868, in the form of a Python script, appeared Saturday on GitHub. "Needs working credentials for the alternate method," the tool's notes read. "Gives you an authenticated session that skipped SAML." The vulnerability can only be exploited if an administrator enables the SAML interface or service for the SSL VPN. Many organizations use SAML to facilitate easier logins for users, by letting them authenticate to an identity provider, or IdP, which then handles single sign-on between that user and multiple service providers, or SPs.

items.title: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
items.summary: Microsoft researchers have discovered “Lazarus,” a backdoor technique that can reprogram dormant neurons in an AI model, causing an otherwise normal AI agent to execute malicious commands when a hidden trigger appears. The threat is especially serious for AI agents with tool or terminal access. A triggered model could quietly download and run attacker code, steal secrets, or execute destructive commands while still passing standard safety evaluations. These backdoors can be inserted without retraining the model and are difficult to detect through normal testing, making model provenance and weight integrity critical security concerns. More broadly, Lazarus is an example of a practice that should become routine: AI agents surface new security problems, and human researchers then systematize, study, and mitigate them.

items.title: GhostFrame: A New ESXi Implant Linked to Settra Ransomware
items.summary: GhostFrame is a previously undocumented post-exploitation framework that gives threat actors extensive control over compromised VMware ESXi environments. Once an attacker gains root-level access to an ESXi host, GhostFrame provides a single interface to access virtual machines running on the hypervisor, harvest credentials, execute commands, and pivot deeper into victim networks. Insikt Group identified GhostFrame being used by TAG-218, a threat activity group whose operations overlap with Settra ransomware. GhostFrame is notable because it allows threat actors to operate from the virtualization layer, where a single compromised ESXi host can provide access to multiple virtual machines and the systems and data they contain. Insikt Group’s findings demonstrate how attackers can use compromised hypervisors as a centralized platform for post-exploitation activity, potentially expanding access across victim environments without compromising each virtual machine individually. The discovery highlights the importance of treating virtualization infrastructure as a high-value target and monitoring ESXi hosts for signs of unauthorized access and post-exploitation activity. Insikt Group identified GhostFrame, a command-and-control (C2) and post-exploitation framework designed to operate on compromised VMware ESXi hypervisors. GhostFrame provides threat actors with a centralized interface to maintain access to ESXi hosts, execute commands, manage virtual machines (VMs), pivot through internal networks, and harvest credentials from Windows systems hosted on the hypervisor. One notable feature is GhostFrame’s ability to operate from the virtualization layer. A single ESXi host can support multiple VMs running critical services within an organization. GhostFrame allows operators with root privileges on the hypervisor to interact with multiple hosted systems from a single point of access instead of requiring separate access to each guest system.

items.title: AI Makes Reverse Engineering Mainstream Software & Malware Far Easier
items.summary: Mainstream software and malware can be reverse-engineered more easily than ever, thanks to artificial intelligence (AI) tools — something that security researchers are warning has implications for cyber defense, intellectual property (IP) theft, and beyond. Household applications typically run on hundreds of thousands, if not millions of lines of code. They incorporate hundreds of third-party libraries, gobs of files, and complex webs of interconnected components. Unpacking and mapping it all is exactly the kind of task that was so difficult before AI, but is now totally in range for even small teams and individuals. Cybersecurity researchers from Intezer recently tested out how easy it is to reverse-engineer software with AI by picking on some high-profile candidates: Slack, Apple's Finder app, and, importantly for security researchers, the Turla malware. Ironically, the malware proved the most difficult to wrangle. They found it only moderately challenging to meaningfully recreate Apple's and Salesforce's proprietary apps from the ground up. "It lowers the bar," Intezer senior security researcher and malware analyst Nicole Fishbein says of AI. "In the past, to reverse-engineer a software, you needed experience. You needed to understand Assembly, and it took a lot of time. Now, I don't want to say anyone [can do it], but it is much easier."

items.title: Exchange for breakfast: Turla’s Cereal tricks are not for kids
items.summary: On a compromised Exchange server, the most interesting activity is not always the message that arrives in a user’s inbox. Somewhere in a national government office, an official sends an email to a colleague at a transnational military alliance. The message goes out through a Microsoft Exchange server, exactly as it should, and nothing looks suspicious. But before the email leaves the building, a piece of code quietly examines it, decides that it is interesting, and sets aside a copy to be forwarded to prying eyes, while the original email continues on its way. On November 28th, 2025, we found the toolset that installs such code on an Exchange server of a governmental organization in Kazakhstan. What initially looked like separate suspicious components soon revealed a previously undocumented toolset: a collection of modular .NET malware designed to run on Microsoft Exchange servers, receive commands, execute them in memory, map the compromised organization, and collect selected email messages. After fine-tuning our detections, we found the same toolset at a governmental organization in Romania – compromised on December 23rd, 2025 – where it was configured to identify emails sent to, or received from, The North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) and European Union (EU). One of the most interesting aspects of this toolset is what we did not find: external command and control (C&C) infrastructure. Instead – adding insult to injury – the victim’s compromised Exchange server is co-opted to act as the C&C infrastructure. We attribute Cereal, with high confidence, to the Russia-aligned APT group Turla, based on the concurrent use of another component publicly linked to Turla and conceptual similarities to older Turla malware. The full technical analysis is available in our white paper.

items.title: Not All That Glitters Is Gold: Tracking CopperDragon’s Sparrow Framework Around the Globe
items.summary: Over the past year, Check Point Research investigated a series of intrusion campaigns targeting several dozens of high-profile organizations across Latin America, Asia, and Europe. These campaigns initially appeared to be independent operations, each using different backdoors, post-exploitation tools and operational pace. However, we identified numerous connections between the tools and their infrastructure which linked them to the same Sparrow malware ecosystem. We track the entity behind these campaigns as CopperDragon, which may serve as a digital quartermaster supporting a number of China-nexus threat actors that use the Sparrow cross-platform malware framework for Linux and Windows. FamousSparrow is a threat actor that was first identified in 2021, whose main backdoor is SparrowDoor. Since then, multiple vendors have reported on related activity and malware variants, including CrowDoor, HemiGate, and TernDoor. Over time, it became apparent that this other activity was not necessarily carried out by the original FamousSparrow group. Instead, reporting pointed to several distinct actors using a shared toolset, potentially supplied by the same entity. These actors include FamousSparrow, Earth Estries, TropicTrooper, UAT-9244, and others. FamousSparrow was previously also linked to Salt Typhoon, but the relationship details remain unclear. Based on the apparent tool-sharing, we began tracking the entity behind the Sparrow framework as CopperDragon, its possible developer and supplier. In this report, we examine three distinct activity clusters targeting major telecommunications providers, government organizations, and military entities. Together, these operations provide a broader view of the connected and evolving espionage ecosystem linked to CopperDragon.

items.title: Google DeepMind melds humans and AI agents to vet Signal's secure messaging techniques
items.summary: Google DeepMind researchers have completed a formal verification of Signal's messaging security, marking what they claim is the first time AI has helped devise a proof that links protocol-level security guarantees to a widely used cryptographic implementation. They did so using AlphaProof Code, a multi-agent framework for formal software specification and verification. AlphaProof Code relies on a human-guided agent that writes a Lean specification, assesses machine code semantics, and crafts an agent-authored proof that the Lean kernel checks against the specification. In this instance, AlphaProof Code verified Signal’s post-quantum PQXDH handshake and Triple Ratchet, thereby validating the design of libsignal's forward secrecy, authentication, post-compromise security, and handshake secrecy. In so doing, the Google/DeepMind team – Swarat Chaudhuri, Andrew Ferraiuolo, Anton Kovsharov, Tej Chajed, Sam Schlesinger, Karn Seth, Jonathan Katz, Charles Sutton, and Pushmeet Kohli – has taken a step toward a challenge the Beneficial AI Foundation issued in April to formally verify the Signal protocol and Signal app with Lean. The result is theoretical in that it assumes perfect cryptography and doesn't guarantee the computational secrecy of bytes. But it's still a meaningful assertion of correctness.

items.title: GhostShares 2: Grok Apps Exposed xAI’s Business Secrets and People’s Private Data
items.summary: We found more than 35,000 apps built with Grok that anyone with the link could open. Among them were SpaceXSI's own sales territory map, an X ad proposal to a U.S. federal agency marked confidential, an ICU patient's lab results, a hospital group's staff list and a timesheet that hands out its employees' passwords. On November 8, 2026, we were working through a long list of web addresses under grok.me, the domain where Grok, the AI assistant from SpaceXSI (the company formerly called xAI), publishes the apps people build with it. Nobody had sent us any of them. We opened the first page of each one once, from the public internet and signed in to nothing, the way anyone would in an incognito window. One address named a new hire and ended in “onboarding plan”. It was the onboarding plan for a new member of SpaceXSI’s own enterprise sales team, marked confidential: the systems to get access to in the first week, internal system addresses, the sales team’s tools, 19 of the company’s internal chat channels, the colleagues to meet and a 30-day plan. Nothing asked us to sign in. We were shocked. The company that makes Grok had its own internal material open to anyone holding the link, and we had never been given it. We call pages like this GhostShares: they open for people who were never given the link, and those people can find them on their own. Last month it was Meta’s Muse. This time it is the apps people make by describing them to Grok and publish from the same chat window.

items.title: Artex: The AI Pen-Test Tool Hackers Turned Into a Weapon
items.summary: AI penetration-testing tool Artex has proven to be a boon for threat actors large and small, taking familiar attacker playbooks and deploying them at machine speeds — ushering in a potentially new era for defenders looking to get ahead of AI-enabled threats. In July, independent developer Autumn-27 published Artex to GitHub, an open source, multiagent AI penetration testing framework written in Go. It is, by intention, a legitimate tool. However, as is so often the case with pen-test tools (such as, famously, Cobalt Strike), threat actors found a way to take advantage of it for malicious use. By late summer and early fall, a range of threat actors were using it as part of their toolkit. Artex is capable of brute-forcing passwords, dumping databases, enumerating and abusing APIs, and more. This positions it for credential compromise and lateral movement in its own right, but the agentic element means Artex can operate at inhuman speeds. Microsoft saw an AI agent move from scanning GitHub for secrets to exfiltrating data from an Azure Key Vault in five minutes, for example. At the end of October, Artex's creator deleted the original GitHub repository due to rampant abuse, but many forks of the tool remain, so the threat remains. But even if all the forks went offline and Artex was no longer a going concern, the underlying threat of frameworks like it is far from over.

items.title: Trump taps Palantir security chief to run battered US cyber defense agency
items.summary: President Donald Trump has nominated Palantir security chief Michael LoSapio to lead CISA, putting an executive from the controversial government supplier in line to run America's civilian cyber defense agency. The nomination, announced on Monday, could end CISA's nearly two-year wait for a Senate-confirmed director following Jen Easterly's departure in January 2025. LoSapio has served as Palantir's CISO since September 2024, having previously led the company's infrastructure and network security team. He first joined the data analytics outfit in 2013, later spent a spell at database company SingleStore, and returned to Palantir in 2017. If confirmed, LoSapio would move from securing Palantir's systems to leading the federal government's main civilian cyber defense agency. CISA protects federal civilian networks and works with critical infrastructure operators, including power, water, and telecommunications providers. LoSapio would be the second person Trump has put forward for the role. His previous pick, Sean Plankey, withdrew in April after spending more than a year awaiting confirmation, with his nomination becoming caught up in a dispute involving Republican Senator Rick Scott over Coast Guard contracting. The nomination arrives late in the congressional calendar. If the Senate does not confirm LoSapio before the current Congress ends, Trump would have to nominate him again for consideration by the incoming Democratic-controlled Senate.
